column1: # Campaign 25 source evidence for the multi-relation SQL-node foundation.

column5: NodeConfig now admits one canonical bounded ordered read-table list and rejects legacy, incomplete, duplicate, oversized, and malformed descriptors before startup; TiDB's full flag, config-file, environment, logging, tracing, bootstrap, and service initialization surface remains open.

The bounded executable validates the exact listener, PD, authentication, connection, packet, and at-most-two signed-BIGINT table inputs it consumes, including TiDB's 4096-column maximum; the general TOML configuration tree, reload, deprecation, and unrelated subsystem settings remain open.
Startup accepts only the real TiKV store and plaintext PD host-port seeds; mock stores, local engines, URI schemes, security configuration, and the broader store registry remain open.

Existing authenticated concurrent-session coverage remains attached to the one shared SQL-node lifecycle while configuration widens to an ordered table list; TLS, all non-native plugins, proxy protocol, capability extensions, and full Go handshake compatibility remain open.

The single process authority retains listener bind, readiness, signal drain, fallible ordered backend shutdown, and success emission while reusable startup-failure and query-completion seams are exposed for F1; status server, Unix sockets, graceful-down orchestration, plugins, and general TiDB server services remain open.

The fixed worker node preserves authenticated connection admission, accounting, cancellation, and exactly-once release across the canonical configuration change; resource groups, dynamic account limits, and distributed connection coordination remain open.

The promoted shared harness now owns default-preserving fixture-preparation, canonical server-argument, and readiness-validation hooks used unchanged by Campaigns 22-24; the broader Go RealTiKV testkit, domain lifecycle, SQL fixtures, and Campaign 25 live join scenario remain open.
